reasons.reproducibility: 58 years of copper treatment of five whole lakes; impossible to repeat.
reasons.effectiveness: Algae recovered within 7-21 days and shifted toward blue-greens.
reasons.environment: Fish kills, copper-laden sediments, loss of macrophytes and invertebrates.

reasons.reproducibility: Lab fluctuation test with ~400 Microcystis cultures; bench scale but needs a purchased strain and a sponsor.
reasons.effectiveness: 10 uM Cu2+ destroyed sensitive cells within days, but resistant mutants regrew in 32 of 198 set-1 cultures.
reasons.cost: Culture, media and copper for hundreds of cultures cost about $150-500.
reasons.time: Resistant cells took about four weeks to regrow under copper.
reasons.environment: Copper persists and repeated dosing selects for resistant toxic Microcystis.

reasons.reproducibility: 85 L aquaria of lake water dosed with copper sulphate; doable with a sponsor for microscopy counts.
reasons.effectiveness: Cyanobacteria were significantly suppressed (n=3), but no bloom was present (7.5% of biomass) and total biomass regrew after 5-8 days in spring.
reasons.cost: Nine aquaria, copper sulphate and phytoplankton counting cost about $150-500.
reasons.time: Biomass declined for 5-8 days and was followed over 27 days.
reasons.environment: 160 ug/L shifted the community to >85% Chlorophyceae and suppressed diatoms and other groups; copper persists.

reasons.reproducibility: Bench Microcystis exposures with MC-LR analysis need ELISA.
reasons.effectiveness: Cellular MC-LR and chl-a declined sigmoidally, but aqueous toxin rose; no percent given.
reasons.environment: Copper added, and toxin moved into the water.

reasons.reproducibility: Beakers of lake water with retail algaecides at label doses; bench scale but needs toxic bloom water and cell counts.
reasons.effectiveness: Replicated (n=3) with controls: copper products cut cells 77-95% at 3 days (SeClear >90%).
reasons.cost: Several algaecides, beakers and microscopy/fluorometry cost about $150-500.
reasons.environment: Copper persists in sediment and copper sulphate (SeClear) released ~91% of microcystin into water at day 1.

reasons.reproducibility: Toxic K. brevis at bloom density; sponsor lab needed.
reasons.effectiveness: 0.31-0.34 mg Cu/L significantly decreased cells in 24 h; no percent given.
reasons.environment: Copper persists; marine non-targets not tested.

reasons.reproducibility: Standard Daphnia magna acute/chronic tests with retail copper algaecides; bench scale and well documented.
reasons.effectiveness: No algae were treated; this is a non-target toxicity study only.
reasons.cost: Daphnia cultures, algaecides and glassware cost about $50-150.
reasons.environment: At 0.4-0.5 mg Cu/L, half the US label maximum, all products cut Daphnia population growth 29-49%.

reasons.reproducibility: Review of in-lake and reservoir chemical treatments; field-scale with permits.
reasons.effectiveness: Copper gave >90% Chl a declines at low-medium densities, but blooms rebounded (mean 14 days, up to six monthly doses).
reasons.cost: Whole-lake algaecide applications cost far over $5,000.
reasons.time: Algaecide declines appear within days, though rebounds follow in ~2 weeks.
reasons.environment: Over 90% of copper ends up in sediment and fauna kills are reported after treatment.

reasons.reproducibility: Tonnes of CuSO4 into a drinking-water reservoir; impossible to repeat.
reasons.effectiveness: 56% surface biomass drop, but blooms returned whenever treatment stopped.
reasons.environment: Tonnes of copper added to a drinking-water reservoir.

reasons.reproducibility: 1 L flasks with retail algaecides at label doses; bench scale but needs Microcystis culture and bloom water.
reasons.effectiveness: Copper products significantly cut cells at 1x and 2x label (n=3), but 0.5x Captain did not differ from control and no percent reduction is given.
reasons.cost: Algaecides, cultures and toxin analysis cost about $150-500.
reasons.environment: Total microcystin often rose 2-10x and moved into the water; copper persists.

reasons.reproducibility: Dose-response of five oxidants on two purchased seawater cultures; sponsor-doable.
reasons.effectiveness: PAA and PMS strong but brief; H2O2 sustained (EC50 6.67-7.08); peroxydisulfate negligible — mixed.
reasons.cost: Two cultures and five oxidants about $150-500.
reasons.environment: Not assessed; oxidants short-lived (no copper used despite file).

reasons.reproducibility: Microcystis culture with 10 mg/L PAA and toxin analysis; sponsor-doable.
reasons.effectiveness: Authors judge PAA impractically slow at neutral/alkaline pH (3-6 h lag).
reasons.environment: <35% of MC-LR released after 12 h; low sudden-release risk; PAA degrades.
